_what: Probe 4 -- NEIGHBOUR EXPANSION FOR SHORT CANDIDATES. A stage-5 forensic case (1568498a) has a SIX-WORD gold turn ('28. Kg3 would be my move.') whose entire topical context lives in adjacent same-session turns. Score such candidates WITH their neighbours.
_why_not_closed_by_prior_neighbour_work: Session M tested neighbour signals as FEATURES/tie-breaks over ALL candidates on the old head and they lost everywhere. Input expansion for SHORT candidates is a different act: a 33-word turn is diluted by neighbours, a 6-word notation fragment can only gain. The gate is length, declared here, not swept.

arms.expansion_pair: candidates <= 16 words are scored by L-2 and L-6 against prev+turn+next (same derived session); others unchanged; shipped pair fusion
arms.expansion_reader_w05: same expansion, plus the half-weight answerability opinion (our measured-best pending config)

declared_constants.expansion: prev + turn + next, same session, both sides present else whichever exist

instrument_gate: baseline reconstruction (no expansion) reproduces the binary's fusion order 229/229 on fit

registered_predictions.expectation_stated_honestly: only ONE of the 16 stage-5 golds is <=16 words, so DIRECT stage-5 yield is small (+1 to +2). The open question is whether expansion recovers cases UPSTREAM (slate/narrowing losses) or harms via dilution elsewhere. Bands cover the uncertainty:

earn_rule: fit R@3 >= 215 AND R@1 >= 179 earns the held-out read (bands registered then, before it)
_also_reported: per-stage recovery census: which slate-lost / narrowing-lost golds become reachable under expansion
